1:48 to 35mm Miniature Scale for 3D Printing

Convert 3D printed tabletop miniatures from 1:48 to 35mm. This STL scale calculator is designed for Warhammer, D&D, and tabletop gaming miniatures.

Slicer Setting

96.0%

Uniform scale (XYZ locked)

Back to all conversions

The math

(35.0mm / 36.5mm) × 100 = 96.0%

Based on 175cm human baseline, eye-level measurement (160cm).

Scale baselines

  • Source eye level33.3mm Eye
  • Target eye level35.0mm Eye
  • Scale factor96.0%

How I got this number

By kitsorix, 3D printing hobbyist

This percentage comes from a 175cm human baseline with eye-level at 160cm. I print the result on my Bambu Lab A1 Mini and measure with digital calipers before I post it. If it looks wrong on my table, I adjust it.

I test every percentage on FDM before publishing. PLA and PETG cool with minimal dimensional change — typically under 0.5%. If a number fails on my machine, I adjust it.

Full methodology →

When you need this

You need this when fitting oversized 1:48 heroes or monsters into a smaller 35mm regiment, or when printing 1:48 STL files for a 35mm game system. At only 4% difference, these scales can mix on the same table without looking wrong. Keep bases consistent and paint styles matched.

Source: 1:48

1:48 is the ratio. Common for vehicles and aircraft. Figures are usually accessories to vehicle kits. Common systems: US O-gauge trains, Bandai Star Wars kits, Aircraft model kits.

Note: 1:48 figures are often molded in soft vinyl rather than hard plastic.

Target: 35mm

35mm is used by Star Wars: Legion, Kingdom Death, Conquest. Popular with painters who want more canvas for freehand detail without entering true bust territory.

Note: 35mm is sometimes marketed as 'true 35mm' (realistic proportions) vs 'heroic 35mm' (exaggerated). Check before mixing.

Print notes

Set your slicer to 96.0%. FDM at 35mm benefits from a 0.2mm nozzle at 0.06mm layer height for faces.
